text.p: Italian bonds and Btp futures slumped with other debt markets on the first trading day of the New Year, sliding through several support levels in a thin market as U.S. T-bonds fell after U.S. December NAPM data triggered a sell-off.

The NAPM index rose to 54.0 against 52.7 in November, well above a forecast 51.5. This and other U.S. data on Tuesday indicated the strength of the U.S. economy could lead to a rise in inflation and a consequent hike in interest rates.
"Btps went into free fall after falling through 128.55, a good technical support level," a London-based trader said.

"We just followed other markets which are not in good shape," he added. The Bpt March contract slid through support at 128.08 and 127.76 to touch a session low at 127.20 before clawing back some ground.
"There are not a lot of operators in the market and they don't want to do much and so there is no real support," he said.
Players were still awaiting an accord in the long-running Italian metalworkers pay dispute with employers after which the market expects to see the Bank of Italy cut its 7.5 percent discount rate.
Formal pay talks are set to resume next week.

"The market is not expecting a move on interest rates until the middle of January, given a positive outcome to the pay talks by then. As long as the markets remain nervous, especially in the U.S., the Btps will suffer," a Milan dealer said.

Dealers noted that the Btp's rise to 130.10 on December 31 was an artificial move given the lack of volume. "The Btps' rise in the last few days was abnormal and now the market's correcting. A price around 128 is more reasonable than 130," one dealer said.
A fall in stock markets following another Wall Street sell-off also added to the general gloom.
